scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Laathi nach is an indigenous cultural dance of the Tharu people in Nepal.

The dance evolved out of the community's close connection to their natural environment, where sticks were used as essential extensions of daily life and as practical defenses against wildlife threats to their crops.
on_screen: Map: Nepal · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Laathi nach takes center stage during the major festival of Dashain, as well as during weddings and celebratory events.
Symbolically, the sticks represent the community's connection to nature and their need to protect themselves and their crops from wild animals.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by participants striking sticks together in coordinated rhythms.
The main physical movement centers on stick-on-stick striking.
While it bears structural similarities to Dandiya Raas from Gujarat, India, it differs in its precise movement patterns and overall style.
Watch for Stick strike.
